question: A man sold an article for ₹219, there by gaining 9.5%. The cost of the article (in ₹) was:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Fractional value of 9.5% = 9.5 ÷ 100 = 19 ÷ 200.

This means if Cost Price (CP) is 200 units, the Profit is 19 units.

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = 200 + 19 = 219 units.

Given SP is 219 units = ₹219 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹1.

Cost Price = 200 units × 1 = ₹200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹219

Gain percentage = 9.5%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 + Gain%)] × SP

 
 CP = 100%
 
 Profit = 9.5%
 

 SP = 109.5% = ₹219

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = [100 ÷ (100 + 9.5)] × 219

⇒ CP = (100 ÷ 109.5) × 219

⇒ CP = (1000 ÷ 1095) × 219

⇒ CP = (200 ÷ 219) × 219

⇒ CP = 200 × 1

⇒ CP = 200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Calculation

When an article is sold at a loss, the Cost Price can be calculated as: CP = [100 ÷ (100 − Loss%)] × SP.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price can also be determined from Marked Price after allowing a discount: SP = MP × [(100 − Discount%) ÷ 100].

Successive Profit/Loss

For successive changes of x% and y%, the net percentage change is given by the effective percentage formula: Net % = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100.
